types.name: HaNode
types.summary: The ha node read model, as returned by the Zabbix API.

fields.name: HaNodeId
fields.summary: The ID of the high availability node, a CUID string.

fields.name: Name
fields.summary: The name of the node, as set by the HANodeName parameter in its server configuration.

fields.name: Address
fields.summary: The IP address or DNS name of the node.

fields.name: Port
fields.summary: The port the node listens on.

fields.name: LastAccess
fields.summary: The time the node last reported to the database, as a Unix timestamp.

fields.name: Status
fields.summary: The node's high-availability state: standby, stopped, unavailable or active (<c>ZBX_NODE_STATUS_*</c>).

types.name: HaNodeGetParameters
types.summary: Query parameters for the ha node .get API method.

fields.name: HaNodeIds
fields.summary: Return only high availability nodes with the given IDs.

fields.name: Filter
fields.summary: Return only nodes whose properties exactly match the given values; the name, address and status properties can be used.

fields.name: Output
fields.summary: The node properties to return, either as a list of property names or as extend for all of them; extend is the default.

fields.name: CountOutput
fields.summary: When true, return the number of matching nodes instead of the records.

fields.name: SortField
fields.summary: The properties to sort nodes by; accepted values are name, lastaccess and status.

fields.name: SortOrder
fields.summary: The direction for each sort property: ASC for ascending, the default, or DESC for descending.

fields.name: Limit
fields.summary: The maximum number of nodes to return.

fields.name: PreserveKeys
fields.summary: When true, return the result as an object keyed by node ID instead of an array.

types.name: HistoryGetParameters
types.summary: Query parameters for the history .get API method.

fields.name: History
fields.summary: Value type of the history to read: float, character, log, unsigned, text or binary; unsigned by default.

fields.name: HostIds
fields.summary: Return only history of items on the given hosts.

fields.name: ItemIds
fields.summary: Limits history to the listed items.

fields.name: TimeFrom
fields.summary: Return only values received at or after the given Unix timestamp.

fields.name: TimeTo
fields.summary: Return only values received at or before the given Unix timestamp.

fields.name: Filter
fields.summary: Exact-match filter: an object whose keys are history record properties and whose values are a single value or an array of accepted values. Text-type properties are not supported.

fields.name: Search
fields.summary: Case-insensitive pattern search: an object whose keys are history record properties and whose values are substrings to look for. By default a value matches anywhere in the property.

fields.name: SearchByAny
fields.summary: If true, return results that match any of the filter or search criteria rather than all of them. Defaults to false.

fields.name: StartSearch
fields.summary: If true, the search criteria match only at the beginning of a property value instead of anywhere in it. Ignored when wildcards are enabled.

fields.name: ExcludeSearch
fields.summary: If true, return the results that do not match the search criteria.

fields.name: SearchWildcardsEnabled
fields.summary: If true, an asterisk in a search value acts as a wildcard. Defaults to false.

fields.name: Output
fields.summary: The history properties to return: a list of property names, or extend for all of them. Defaults to extend.

fields.name: CountOutput
fields.summary: If true, return the number of matching records instead of the records themselves.

fields.name: SortField
fields.summary: Properties to sort the result by. Allowed values: itemid, clock, ns. Without it the result is unsorted.

fields.name: SortOrder
fields.summary: Sort direction, ascending or descending; when a list is given, each entry applies to the sort field at the same position. Defaults to ascending.

fields.name: Limit
fields.summary: Maximum number of records to return.

fields.name: Editable
fields.summary: If true, return only history of items the user has write permission to. Defaults to false.

fields.name: MaxValueSize
fields.summary: 8.0, binary and JSON history only (any other value type is refused): the length at which a value is cut, 1 to 128 MiB, 64 KiB when absent; <c>ZabbixOptional<int>.Null</c> asks for the whole value (<c>CHistory.php</c>).

fields.name: ItemId
fields.summary: ID of the item the value is for; give it, or the host and the key.

fields.name: Host
fields.summary: Technical name of the host that owns the item. Required, together with the key, when no item ID is given.

fields.name: Key
fields.summary: Key of the item that receives the value. Required, together with the host, when no item ID is given.

fields.name: Value
fields.summary: Value to send to the item. Required.
fields.json: the API validates it as VALUE

fields.name: Clock
fields.summary: Time of the value, as a Unix timestamp; the server's time when left out.

fields.name: Ns
fields.summary: Nanoseconds of the value's time.

types.name: HistoryPushResult
types.summary: What <c>history.push</c> answers: <c>success</c>, and one row per pushed value, in order.

fields.name: Response
fields.summary: <c>success</c> when the server took the request (a refused value is a row with an <c>error</c>).

fields.name: Values
fields.summary: One row per pushed value, in the order they were sent.

types.name: HistoryPushResultValue
types.summary: One pushed value's outcome: the item it went to, and why it was refused when it was.

fields.name: ItemId
fields.summary: The item the value was for, written to unless <see cref="Error"/> is set; absent when no item matched the host and key, or the caller may not write to it (<c>trapper_history_push.c</c>).

fields.name: Error
fields.summary: Why the value was refused (the item's allowed hosts, its type, the value); absent when it was stored.

types.name: HistoryRecord
types.summary: The history record read model, as returned by the Zabbix API.

fields.name: Value
fields.summary: Value that was received. The API returns it as a string whatever the item's type of information.

fields.name: ItemId
fields.summary: ID of the item the value belongs to.

fields.name: Clock
fields.summary: Time the value was collected, as a Unix timestamp.

fields.name: Ns
fields.summary: Nanoseconds of the time the value was collected.

fields.name: Timestamp
fields.summary: Log entry's own timestamp (LOG history only).

fields.name: Source
fields.summary: Log entry source, e.g. the Windows eventlog source (LOG history only).

fields.name: Severity
fields.summary: Log entry severity (LOG history only).

fields.name: LogEventId
fields.summary: Windows eventlog event id (LOG history only).

fields.name: HostId
fields.summary: ID of the host.

fields.name: TechnicalName
fields.summary: Technical name of the host, unique among hosts and templates; an active agent's Hostname must match it.

fields.name: MonitoredBy
fields.summary: What monitors the host: Zabbix server, a single proxy, or a proxy group.

fields.name: ProxyId
fields.summary: ID of the proxy that monitors the host when it is monitored by a proxy; 0 otherwise.

fields.name: ProxyGroupId
fields.summary: ID of the proxy group that monitors the host, when the host is monitored by a proxy group; otherwise 0.

fields.name: AssignedProxyId
fields.summary: ID of the proxy that Zabbix server picked from the proxy group to monitor the host; 0 when the host is not monitored by a proxy group. Read-only.

fields.name: Status
fields.summary: Whether the host is monitored or not; a disabled host is not polled.

fields.name: IpmiAuthtype
fields.summary: IPMI authentication algorithm used to reach the host, such as none, MD2, MD5, straight, OEM or RMCP+, or the interface default.

fields.name: IpmiPrivilege
fields.summary: IPMI privilege level requested from the BMC: callback, user, operator, admin or OEM.

fields.name: IpmiUsername
fields.summary: User name for IPMI checks on the host.

fields.name: IpmiPassword
fields.summary: Password for IPMI checks on the host.

fields.name: MaintenanceId
fields.summary: The maintenance that covers the host right now, by ID; 0 when the host is not in maintenance. Read-only.

fields.name: MaintenanceStatus
fields.summary: Whether the host is in maintenance now.

fields.name: MaintenanceType
fields.summary: Whether data is still collected during the maintenance currently in effect on the host. Read-only.

fields.name: MaintenanceFrom
fields.summary: Unix timestamp at which the maintenance currently in effect on the host started. Read-only.

fields.name: VisibleName
fields.summary: Visible name of the host. When empty on create, the server uses the technical host name.

fields.name: Flags
fields.summary: What low-level discovery made of the host: a plain host, a discovery rule or prototype, or one created by discovery.

fields.name: Description
fields.summary: Free-form text describing the host.

fields.name: Granularity
fields.summary: The fixed length of each aggregation bucket in the processing window of telemetry query items, as a time unit from 1 second to 1 day. The default is 15s.

fields.name: SearchWildcardsEnabled
fields.summary: If true, an asterisk in a search value acts as a wildcard. Defaults to false.

fields.name: MediaTypeId

fields.name: SmtpEmail

fields.name: SmtpPort

fields.name: MaxAttempts

fields.name: AttemptInterval

fields.name: ContentType

fields.name: MessageFormat

fields.name: Script

fields.name: ProcessTags

fields.name: Parameters

fields.name: MessageTemplates

fields.name: TokenUrl

fields.name: TokensStatus

fields.name: AccessToken

fields.name: AccessTokenUpdated

fields.name: AccessExpiresIn
fields.summary: The lifetime of the OAuth access token, in seconds.

fields.name: RefreshToken
fields.summary: The OAuth refresh token used to obtain a new access token.

types.name: NetworkDiscoveryCheck
types.summary: The network discovery check read model, as returned by the Zabbix API.

fields.name: NetworkDiscoveryCheckId
fields.summary: Discovery check ID.

fields.name: NetworkDiscoveryRuleId
fields.summary: The owning discovery rule, by ID.

fields.name: Type
fields.summary: The service the check probes: a TCP service such as SSH, LDAP, SMTP, FTP, HTTP, HTTPS, POP, NNTP, IMAP or Telnet, a generic TCP port, the Zabbix agent, SNMPv1, SNMPv2c, SNMPv3 or ICMP ping.

fields.name: Key
fields.summary: The item key for Zabbix agent checks, or the SNMP object identifier for SNMP checks.

fields.name: SnmpCommunity
fields.summary: The SNMP community used by SNMPv1 and SNMPv2c checks.

fields.name: Ports
fields.summary: The ports to probe, as a comma-separated list of ports and port ranges.

fields.name: Snmpv3SecurityName
fields.summary: The security name used by SNMPv3 checks.

fields.name: Snmpv3SecurityLevel
fields.summary: The security level of SNMPv3 checks: noAuthNoPriv, authNoPriv or authPriv.

fields.name: Snmpv3AuthPassphrase
fields.summary: The authentication passphrase of SNMPv3 checks that use authentication.

fields.name: Snmpv3PrivPassphrase
fields.summary: The privacy passphrase of SNMPv3 checks that use encryption.

fields.name: Uniq
fields.summary: Whether the value of this check identifies a unique device: 0 no, 1 yes. Supported only for Zabbix agent and SNMP checks.

fields.name: Snmpv3AuthProtocol
fields.summary: The authentication protocol of SNMPv3 checks: MD5, SHA1, SHA224, SHA256, SHA384 or SHA512.

fields.name: Snmpv3PrivProtocol
fields.summary: The privacy protocol of SNMPv3 checks: DES, AES128, AES192, AES256, AES192C or AES256C.

fields.name: Snmpv3ContextName
fields.summary: The context name used by SNMPv3 checks.

fields.name: HostSource
fields.summary: Where the host name of a discovered host comes from: 1 DNS name, 2 IP address, 3 the value returned by this check.

fields.name: NameSource
fields.summary: Where the visible name of a discovered host comes from: 0 not specified, 1 DNS name, 2 IP address, 3 the value returned by this check.

fields.name: AllowRedirect
fields.summary: How ICMP ping checks treat a redirect reply: 0 as a failure, 1 as a success.

fields.name: Drules
fields.summary: What <c>selectDRules</c> adds.

types.summary: Query parameters for the network discovery check .get API method.

fields.name: NetworkDiscoveryCheckIds
fields.summary: Limits the result to the discovery checks whose IDs are listed.

fields.name: NetworkDiscoveryRuleIds
fields.summary: Keeps discovery checks owned by any of the listed discovery rules.

fields.name: DserviceIds
fields.summary: Return only discovery checks of the rules that discovered the given services.

fields.name: Editable
fields.summary: When true, return only discovery checks the caller has write permission for.

fields.name: Filter
fields.summary: Return only discovery checks whose properties exactly match the given values; each key is a property name and each value is a single value or an array of accepted values.

fields.name: Search
fields.summary: Return only discovery checks whose string properties match the given patterns; by default a property matches when it contains the text, without regard to case.

fields.name: SearchByAny
fields.summary: When true, return discovery checks that match any of the search patterns instead of all of them.

fields.name: StartSearch
fields.summary: When true, a search pattern matches only at the start of the property value instead of anywhere in it.

fields.name: ExcludeSearch
fields.summary: When true, return discovery checks that do not match the search patterns.

fields.name: SearchWildcardsEnabled
fields.summary: When true, an asterisk in a search pattern matches any sequence of characters.

fields.name: Output
fields.summary: The discovery check properties to return, either as a list of property names or as extend for all of them; extend is the default.

fields.name: SelectNetworkDiscoveryRules
fields.summary: Return the discovery rule each check belongs to in the drules property.

fields.name: CountOutput
fields.summary: When true, return the number of matching discovery checks instead of the records.

fields.name: GroupCount
fields.summary: When true together with the count option, return the counts grouped by the ID filter that was used.

fields.name: PreserveKeys
fields.summary: When true, return the result as an object keyed by discovery check ID instead of an array.

fields.name: SortField
fields.summary: The properties to sort discovery checks by; accepted values are dcheckid and druleid.

fields.name: SortOrder
fields.summary: The direction for each sort property: ASC for ascending, the default, or DESC for descending.

fields.name: Limit
fields.summary: The maximum number of discovery checks to return.

fields.name: LimitSelects
fields.summary: The maximum number of records each related-object selection returns.

fields.name: Type
fields.summary: The kind of service that the check probes.

fields.name: Key
fields.summary: The item key queried by Zabbix agent checks, or the OID queried by SNMP checks.

fields.name: SnmpCommunity
fields.summary: The SNMP community string; required for SNMPv1 and SNMPv2c checks.

fields.name: Ports
fields.summary: The ports or port ranges that the check probes, as a comma-separated list such as 22,80-82.

fields.name: Snmpv3SecurityName
fields.summary: The SNMPv3 security name.

fields.name: Snmpv3SecurityLevel
fields.summary: The SNMPv3 security level, which decides whether authentication and privacy are used.

fields.name: Snmpv3AuthPassphrase
fields.summary: The SNMPv3 authentication passphrase.

fields.name: Snmpv3PrivPassphrase
fields.summary: The SNMPv3 privacy passphrase.

fields.name: Unique
fields.summary: Whether this check is the uniqueness criterion that identifies a device: 0 no, 1 yes. Only one check in a rule can be the criterion.

fields.name: Snmpv3Authprotocol
fields.summary: The SNMPv3 authentication protocol.

fields.name: Snmpv3Privprotocol
fields.summary: The SNMPv3 privacy protocol.

fields.name: Snmpv3Contextname
fields.summary: The SNMPv3 context name.

fields.name: HostSource

fields.name: NameSource

fields.name: AllowRedirect
fields.summary: Whether a host that answers an ICMP ping from a different IP address than the one pinged counts as up: 0 no, 1 yes. Used only by ICMP ping checks.

fields.name: NetworkDiscoveryRuleId
fields.summary: The network discovery rule, by ID.

fields.name: ProxyId
fields.summary: ID of the proxy that runs the discovery; 0 for the server.

fields.name: Name
fields.summary: Network discovery rule name; no two rules may share it.

fields.name: IpRange
fields.summary: Addresses to scan, as a comma-separated list of single IP addresses, ranges such as 192.168.1.1-255, and CIDR subnets; each range may cover at most 65536 addresses.

fields.name: Delay
fields.summary: How often the rule runs, as a time unit with a suffix (30s, 1h) or a user macro.

fields.name: Severities

fields.name: EventIdTo
fields.summary: Return only problems whose event ID is less than or equal to the given ID.

fields.name: TimeFrom
fields.summary: Keeps problems whose creation time is no earlier than this Unix time.

fields.name: TimeTo
fields.summary: Keeps problems whose creation time is no later than the given Unix time.

fields.name: Acknowledged
fields.summary: When true, return only acknowledged problems; when false, only unacknowledged ones.

fields.name: Action
fields.summary: Return only problems on which all of the given update actions were performed, given as a combination of action flags such as acknowledge, suppress or severity change.

fields.name: ActionUserIds
fields.summary: Return only problems updated by the given users.

fields.name: Suppressed
fields.summary: When true, return only suppressed problems; when false, only problems that are not suppressed.

fields.name: Symptom
fields.summary: When true, return only symptom problems; when false, only cause problems.

fields.name: Recent
fields.summary: When true, also return problems resolved within the period for which resolved problems stay displayed; otherwise only unresolved problems are returned.

fields.name: EvalType

fields.name: Tags

fields.name: ExcludeSearch

fields.name: SearchWildcardsEnabled

fields.name: CountOutput

types.name: SlaCreateRequest
types.summary: Write-request payload for the sla .create API method.

fields.name: Name
fields.summary: Name of the SLA.

fields.name: Period
fields.summary: Reporting period of the SLA: daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly or annually.

fields.name: Slo
fields.summary: Service level objective as a percentage from 0 to 100 with up to four decimal places; the SLA is not met when the service level indicator falls below it.

fields.name: EffectiveDate
fields.summary: Date from which the SLA applies, as a Unix timestamp in UTC.

fields.name: Timezone
fields.summary: Time zone used for reporting, such as Europe/London or UTC.

fields.name: Status
fields.summary: Enabled/disabled status. Wire field status. Left out, the server stores <c>ZBX_SLA_STATUS_ENABLED</c> (the <c>sla.status</c> default).

fields.name: Description
fields.summary: Free-form description of the SLA.

fields.name: ServiceTags
fields.summary: Service tags that select the services the SLA covers; each has a tag name, an operator (equals or contains) and a value.

fields.name: Schedule
fields.summary: Recurring weekly periods during which the services are expected to be up, each given as seconds from the start of the week (Sunday); an empty schedule means always.

fields.name: ExcludedDowntimes
fields.summary: Named one-off periods, given as Unix timestamps, that are left out of the SLA calculation, such as planned maintenance.

fields.name: Name
fields.summary: Name of the excluded downtime.

fields.name: PeriodFrom
fields.summary: Start of the excluded downtime, as a Unix timestamp.

fields.name: PeriodTo
fields.summary: End of the excluded downtime, as a Unix timestamp.

types.name: SlaGetParameters
types.summary: Query parameters for the sla .get API method.

fields.name: SlaIds
fields.summary: Limits the result to the SLAs whose IDs are listed.

fields.name: Evaltype
fields.summary: How the service tag conditions combine: And/Or (the default), where conditions on the same tag name are joined with Or and different names with And, or Or, where any condition is enough.

fields.name: ServiceTags
fields.summary: Return only SLAs whose service tags match the given conditions; each condition has a tag name, a value and an operator (contains, equals, does not contain, does not equal, exists or does not exist).

fields.name: ServiceIds
fields.summary: Return only SLAs that cover the given services.

fields.name: Filter
fields.summary: Return only SLAs whose properties exactly match the given values; each key is a property name and each value is a single value or an array of accepted values.

fields.name: Search
fields.summary: Return only SLAs whose properties contain the given text; matching is case-insensitive and substring-based unless startSearch or searchWildcardsEnabled changes it.

fields.name: SearchByAny
fields.summary: When true, return objects that match any of the search criteria instead of all of them.

fields.name: StartSearch
fields.summary: When true, search values match only at the beginning of a property instead of anywhere in it.

fields.name: ExcludeSearch
fields.summary: When true, return the objects that do not match the search criteria.

fields.name: SearchWildcardsEnabled
fields.summary: When true, an asterisk in a search value matches any sequence of characters.

fields.name: Output
fields.summary: Properties of the SLAs to return: a list of property names, or extend for all properties.

fields.name: CountOutput
fields.summary: When true, return the number of matching SLAs instead of the records themselves.

fields.name: SelectServiceTags
fields.summary: Return a service_tags property with the service tags of the SLA; supports count.

fields.name: SelectSchedule
fields.summary: Return a schedule property with the weekly schedule of the SLA; supports count.

fields.name: SelectExcludedDowntimes
fields.summary: Return an excluded_downtimes property with the excluded downtimes of the SLA; supports count.

fields.name: SortField
fields.summary: Properties to sort the result by; supported values are slaid, name, period, slo, effective_date, timezone, status and description.

fields.name: SortOrder
fields.summary: Sort direction for each sort field: ASC for ascending (the default) or DESC for descending.

fields.name: Limit
fields.summary: Maximum number of records to return.

fields.name: Editable
fields.summary: When true, return only SLAs that the user has write permission on.

fields.name: PreserveKeys
fields.summary: When true, return the result as an object keyed by ID instead of an array.

fields.name: SlaId
fields.summary: ID of the SLA to report the service level indicator for.

fields.name: PeriodFrom
fields.summary: Unix time of the start of the reporting range, inclusive.

fields.name: PeriodTo
fields.summary: Unix time of the end of the reporting range, inclusive.

fields.name: Periods
fields.summary: Number of reporting periods to return, from 1 to 100; when omitted, up to 20 periods are returned, or up to 100 when both ends of the range are given.

fields.name: ServiceIds
fields.summary: IDs of the services to report on; when omitted, all services covered by the SLA are reported.

fields.summary: How the tag was created: 0 when it was added manually, 1 when it was created automatically by low-level discovery; returned for hosts and triggers only.

types.name: TagFilter
types.summary: A condition on an object's tags that a <c>.get</c> filters by.

fields.name: Tag

fields.name: Operator
fields.summary: How the tag is matched: whether the value is contained in or equal to the tag value, the negations of those, or whether the tag exists or does not exist; the server uses a contains match when omitted.

fields.name: Value
fields.summary: Value to compare with the tag value using the chosen operator; ignored when only the existence of the tag is tested.

fields.name: Top

fields.name: MediaAlerts

fields.name: SourceAlerts

fields.summary: How the tag conditions combine: And/Or (the default), where conditions on the same tag name are joined with Or and different names with And, or Or, where any condition is enough.

fields.name: Tags
fields.summary: Filters templates by tag; each condition pairs a tag name and value with an operator (contains, equals, does not contain, does not equal, exists or does not exist). With no conditions, every template matches.

fields.name: Filter
fields.summary: Return only templates whose properties exactly match the given values; each key is a property name and each value is a single value or an array of accepted values.

fields.name: Search
fields.summary: Return only templates whose properties contain the given text; matching is case-insensitive and substring-based unless startSearch or searchWildcardsEnabled changes it.

fields.summary: When true, return objects that match any of the search criteria instead of all of them.

fields.summary: When true, search values match only at the beginning of a property instead of anywhere in it.

fields.name: ExcludeSearch
fields.summary: When true, return the objects that do not match the search criteria.

fields.summary: When used with countOutput, return one count for each related object the query is filtered by (for example, one per host) instead of a single total.

types.name: TokenGetParameters
types.summary: Query parameters for the token .get API method.

fields.name: TokenIds
fields.summary: Limits the result to the tokens whose IDs are listed.

fields.name: UserIds
fields.summary: Return only tokens that belong to the given users.

fields.name: TokenValue
fields.summary: Return only the token with the given 64-character authentication string.

fields.name: ValidAt
fields.summary: Return only tokens that have not expired at the given time, as a Unix timestamp.

fields.name: ExpiredAt
fields.summary: Return only tokens that have expired at the given time, as a Unix timestamp.

fields.name: Filter
fields.summary: Return only tokens whose properties exactly match the given values; each key is a property name and each value is a single value or an array of accepted values.

fields.name: Search
fields.summary: Return only tokens whose string properties match the given patterns; by default a property matches when it contains the text, without regard to case.

fields.name: SearchByAny
fields.summary: When true, return tokens that match any of the search patterns instead of all of them.

fields.name: StartSearch
fields.summary: When true, a search pattern matches only at the start of the property value instead of anywhere in it.

fields.name: ExcludeSearch
fields.summary: When true, return tokens that do not match the search patterns.

fields.name: SearchWildcardsEnabled
fields.summary: When true, an asterisk in a search pattern matches any sequence of characters.

fields.name: Output
fields.summary: The token properties to return, either as a list of property names or as extend for all of them; extend is the default.

fields.name: CountOutput
fields.summary: When true, return the number of matching tokens instead of the records.

fields.name: SortField
fields.summary: The properties to sort tokens by; accepted values are tokenid, name, lastaccess, status, expires_at and created_at.

fields.name: SortOrder
fields.summary: The direction for each sort property: ASC for ascending, the default, or DESC for descending.

fields.name: Limit
fields.summary: The maximum number of tokens to return.

fields.name: PreserveKeys
fields.summary: When true, return the result as an object keyed by token ID instead of an array.

fields.name: TokenId
fields.summary: The ID of the API token.

fields.name: Name
fields.summary: The name of the token, unique among the tokens of the same user.

fields.name: Description
fields.summary: A free-text description of the token.

fields.name: Status
fields.summary: Whether the token is enabled; a disabled token cannot authenticate requests.

fields.name: ExpiresAt
fields.summary: The time the token expires, as a Unix timestamp; 0 means it never expires.

fields.name: Clock
fields.summary: Start of the hour the trend covers, as a Unix timestamp.

fields.name: Num

fields.name: ValueMin

fields.name: ValueAvg

types.name: Trigger
types.summary: The trigger read model, as returned by the Zabbix API.

fields.name: TriggerId
fields.summary: ID of the trigger.

fields.name: Expression
fields.summary: Problem expression that the server evaluates to decide whether the trigger is in the problem state; item references appear as function IDs unless expandExpression is requested.

fields.name: Name
fields.summary: Name of the trigger, as the frontend shows it; it may contain macros. The API calls it <c>description</c>; the free-text description is <see cref="Description"/>.

fields.name: Url
fields.summary: URL associated with the trigger and shown with its problems; user macros allowed.

fields.name: Status
fields.summary: Whether the trigger is enabled; a disabled trigger is not evaluated.

fields.name: Value
fields.summary: Current state of the trigger: OK or problem.

fields.name: Priority
fields.summary: Severity of the trigger, from not classified to disaster. Defaults to not classified.

fields.name: LastChange
fields.summary: Unix timestamp of the trigger's most recent state change.

fields.name: Description
fields.summary: Description of the trigger, the free text the frontend shows as its description; it may contain macros. The API calls it <c>comments</c>; the trigger's name is <see cref="Name"/>.

fields.name: Error
fields.summary: Why the server could not evaluate the trigger; empty while its state is normal.

fields.name: TemplateId
fields.summary: ID of the trigger in the template it was inherited from; 0 when it was not inherited.

fields.name: Type
fields.summary: Whether the trigger generates a single problem event or a new problem event on every evaluation that results in a problem. Defaults to a single event.

fields.name: State
fields.summary: Whether the server can evaluate the trigger: normal or unknown.

fields.name: Flags
fields.summary: What low-level discovery made of the trigger: a plain trigger, a discovery rule or prototype, or one created by discovery.

fields.name: RecoveryMode
fields.summary: How the trigger decides that a problem is resolved: when the problem expression is false, when the recovery expression is true, or never (problems are only closed manually or by correlation). Defaults to the problem expression.

fields.name: RecoveryExpression
fields.summary: Expression that resolves the problem when it evaluates to true; used only when the recovery mode is the recovery expression.

fields.name: CorrelationMode
fields.summary: Which problems an OK event closes: all problems of the trigger, or only problems whose value for the correlation tag matches. Defaults to all problems.

fields.name: CorrelationTag
fields.summary: Tag whose value must match for an OK event to close a problem when the correlation mode is tag based.

fields.name: ManualClose
fields.summary: Whether users may close the trigger's problems manually. Defaults to not allowed.

fields.name: Opdata
fields.summary: Operational data shown with the trigger's problems; it may contain macros.

fields.name: EventName
fields.summary: Template for the names of the events the trigger generates, with macros allowed; when empty, the trigger name is used.

fields.name: UrlName
fields.summary: Label shown for the trigger URL; user macros allowed.

fields.name: Uuid
fields.summary: Universally unique identifier of the trigger, which matches it to the same trigger when a configuration is exported and imported.

fields.name: Groups
fields.summary: What <c>selectGroups</c> adds.

fields.name: Hostgroups
fields.summary: What <c>selectHostGroups</c> adds.

fields.name: Templategroups
fields.summary: What <c>selectTemplateGroups</c> adds.

fields.name: Hosts
fields.summary: Hosts or templates the trigger belongs to; returned when selectHosts is requested.

fields.name: Items
fields.summary: Items used in the trigger expressions; returned when selectItems is requested.

fields.name: Functions
fields.summary: Functions used in the trigger expressions; returned when selectFunctions is requested.

fields.name: Dependencies
fields.summary: Triggers this trigger depends on; returned when selectDependencies is requested.

fields.name: DiscoveryRule
fields.summary: What <c>selectDiscoveryRule</c> adds.

fields.name: LastEvent
fields.summary: What <c>selectLastEvent</c> adds.

fields.name: Tags
fields.summary: Tags of the trigger; returned when selectTags is requested.

fields.name: TriggerDiscovery
fields.summary: What <c>selectTriggerDiscovery</c> adds.

fields.name: DiscoveryData
fields.summary: What <c>selectDiscoveryData</c> adds.

fields.name: InheritedTags
fields.summary: What <c>selectInheritedTags</c> adds.

fields.summary: Enabled/disabled status. Wire field status. Left out, the server stores <c>TRIGGER_STATUS_ENABLED</c> (the <c>triggers.status</c> default).

fields.name: Url
fields.summary: URL associated with the trigger and shown with its problems; user macros allowed.

types.name: TriggerDiscoveryData

types.name: TriggerGetParameters
types.summary: Query parameters for the trigger .get API method.

fields.name: GroupIds
fields.summary: Keeps triggers owned by a host or template that is a member of any listed host or template group.

fields.name: TemplateIds
fields.summary: Keeps triggers owned by any of the listed templates.

fields.name: HostIds
fields.summary: Keeps triggers defined on any of the listed hosts or templates.

fields.name: TriggerIds
fields.summary: Limits the result to the triggers whose IDs are listed.

fields.name: ItemIds
fields.summary: Keeps triggers that reference any of the listed items.

fields.name: Functions
fields.summary: Return only triggers whose expressions use the given functions, such as last or avg.

fields.name: Inherited
fields.summary: When true, return only triggers inherited from a template; when false, only triggers that are not inherited.

fields.name: Dependent
fields.summary: When true, return only triggers that depend on other triggers; when false, only triggers without dependencies.

fields.name: Templated
fields.summary: When true, return only triggers that belong to templates; when false, only triggers on hosts.

fields.name: Monitored
fields.summary: Return only enabled triggers whose items are all enabled and whose hosts are all monitored.

fields.name: Active
fields.summary: Keeps triggers that are enabled and sit on monitored hosts.

fields.name: Maintenance
fields.summary: When true, return only enabled triggers on hosts in maintenance; when false, only enabled triggers on hosts not in maintenance.

fields.name: WithUnacknowledgedEvents
fields.summary: Keeps triggers with problem events nobody has acknowledged.

fields.name: WithAcknowledgedEvents
fields.summary: Return only triggers whose problem events are all acknowledged.

fields.name: WithLastEventUnacknowledged
fields.summary: Return only triggers whose most recent problem event is unacknowledged.

fields.name: SkipDependent
fields.summary: Skip triggers that depend on another trigger which is in the problem state.

fields.name: Editable
fields.summary: When true, return only objects the calling user has write permission to.

fields.name: LastChangeSince
fields.summary: Keeps triggers whose state changed later than the given Unix timestamp.

fields.name: LastChangeTill
fields.summary: Keeps triggers whose last state change, a Unix timestamp, is earlier than this value.

fields.name: Group
fields.summary: Return only triggers that belong to hosts in the host group with the given name.

fields.name: Host
fields.summary: Keeps triggers owned by the host whose technical name is given.

fields.name: OnlyTrue
fields.summary: Return only triggers that are in the problem state or that recently returned to OK, within the period configured for showing OK triggers.

fields.name: MinSeverity
fields.summary: Return only triggers with a severity equal to or higher than the given one (0 not classified to 5 disaster).

fields.name: EvalType
fields.summary: How the Tags conditions combine: And/Or (the default) or Or.

fields.name: Tags
fields.summary: Return only triggers whose tags match the given conditions, each with a tag name, an operator and a value.

fields.name: Filter
fields.summary: Return only results whose properties exactly match the given values; each key is a property name and each value is a single value or an array of accepted values.

fields.name: Search
fields.summary: Return only results whose given text properties contain the given strings; matching is case-insensitive.

fields.name: SearchByAny

fields.name: ExcludeSearch

fields.name: SearchWildcardsEnabled

fields.name: ExpandDescription

fields.name: ExpandComment
fields.summary: Set to true to resolve macros in the description.

fields.name: ExpandExpression

fields.name: Output

fields.name: SelectGroups

fields.name: SelectHostGroups

fields.name: SelectTemplateGroups

fields.name: SelectHosts

fields.name: SelectItems

fields.name: SelectFunctions

fields.name: SelectDependencies

fields.name: SelectDiscoveryRule

fields.name: SelectLastEvent

fields.name: SelectTags

fields.name: SelectTriggerDiscovery
fields.summary: Deprecated; returns the discovery data of a discovered trigger in the triggerDiscovery property. Use SelectDiscoveryData instead.

fields.name: CountOutput
fields.summary: When true, return the number of matching records instead of the records themselves.

fields.name: GroupCount

fields.name: PreserveKeys

fields.name: SortField

fields.name: SortOrder

fields.name: Limit

fields.name: LimitSelects

fields.name: SelectDiscoveryData

fields.name: MaintenanceIds

fields.name: InheritedTags

fields.name: ObjectType
fields.summary: The kind of object that created the event: 0 trigger, 1 discovered host, 2 discovered service, 3 autoregistered host, 4 item, 5 low-level discovery rule, 6 service.

fields.name: ObjectId

fields.name: Clock

fields.name: Acknowledged

fields.name: Ns

fields.name: Name

fields.name: Severity

fields.name: TriggerId

fields.name: Status
fields.summary: Trigger prototype status, enabled by default; a disabled prototype yields no discovered triggers.

fields.name: Priority

fields.name: Description

fields.name: TemplateId
fields.summary: ID of the trigger prototype in the template it was inherited from; 0 when it was not inherited.

fields.name: Type
fields.summary: Whether discovered triggers generate a new problem event on every evaluation in the problem state, or only one event per problem. Single event by default.

fields.name: Flags
fields.summary: What low-level discovery made of the trigger prototype: a plain trigger prototype, a discovery rule or prototype, or one created by discovery.

fields.name: RecoveryMode
fields.summary: How discovered triggers return to OK: by the problem expression (the default), by a separate recovery expression, or never automatically.

fields.name: RecoveryExpression
fields.summary: The expression that resolves the problem when the recovery mode uses a recovery expression; it must reference at least one item prototype.

fields.name: CorrelationMode
fields.summary: Which problems an OK event closes: all problems of the trigger (the default), or only those whose correlation tag values match.

fields.name: CorrelationTag
fields.summary: The tag whose value must match for an OK event to close a problem when correlation by tag is used.

fields.name: ManualClose
fields.summary: Whether users can close problems of discovered triggers manually. Not allowed by default.

fields.name: Opdata
fields.summary: The operational data shown with problems, usually item values referenced through macros.

fields.name: Discover

fields.name: EventName

fields.name: Uuid

fields.name: UrlName
fields.summary: Link text shown for the URL of triggers made from this prototype.

types.name: TriggerPrototypeGetParameters
types.summary: Query parameters for the trigger prototype .get API method.

fields.name: GroupIds
fields.summary: Keeps trigger prototypes whose hosts or templates are members of the listed host groups or template groups.

fields.name: TemplateIds
fields.summary: Keeps trigger prototypes owned by any of the listed templates.

fields.name: HostIds
fields.summary: Keeps trigger prototypes owned by any of the listed hosts or templates.

fields.name: TriggerIds
fields.summary: Limits the result to the trigger prototypes whose IDs are listed.

fields.name: ItemIds
fields.summary: Return only trigger prototypes whose expressions use the given items or item prototypes.

fields.name: DiscoveryIds
fields.summary: Return only trigger prototypes that belong to the given low-level discovery rules.

fields.name: Functions
fields.summary: Return only trigger prototypes whose expressions use the given trigger functions.

fields.name: Inherited
fields.summary: When true, return only trigger prototypes inherited from a template; when false, only those that are not inherited.

fields.name: Templated
fields.summary: When true, return only trigger prototypes that belong to templates; when false, only those that belong to hosts.

fields.name: Monitored
fields.summary: Keeps enabled trigger prototypes on monitored hosts whose items are all enabled.

fields.name: Active
fields.summary: Keeps enabled trigger prototypes on monitored hosts only.

fields.name: Maintenance
fields.summary: When true, return only enabled trigger prototypes of hosts in maintenance; when false, only those of hosts not in maintenance.

fields.name: Editable
fields.summary: Whether to return only trigger prototypes that the current user is allowed to change.

fields.name: Group
fields.summary: Filters trigger prototypes by the name of a host group or template group that holds their host or template.

fields.name: Host
fields.summary: Return only trigger prototypes that belong to the host or template with the given technical name.

fields.name: MinSeverity
fields.summary: Return only trigger prototypes whose severity is at least the given value, from 0 (not classified) to 5 (disaster).

fields.name: Filter
fields.summary: Return only trigger prototypes whose properties exactly match the given values; besides the object properties it accepts host (the technical host name) and hostid.

fields.name: Search
fields.summary: Return only trigger prototypes whose properties contain the given strings, using a case-insensitive substring match by default; each key is a property name.

fields.name: SearchByAny
fields.summary: Whether an object that matches any one of the search or filter criteria is returned; by default every criterion must match.

fields.name: StartSearch
fields.summary: Whether the search strings must match the beginning of the property value rather than any part of it.

fields.name: ExcludeSearch
fields.summary: Whether to return the objects that do not match the search criteria instead of those that do.

fields.name: SearchWildcardsEnabled
fields.summary: Whether an asterisk in a search string acts as a wildcard that matches any sequence of characters.

fields.name: ExpandExpression
fields.summary: Whether function references and macros in the returned expressions are expanded.

fields.name: Output
fields.summary: Which properties to return for each object, given as a list of property names or extend to return all of them.

fields.name: SelectGroups
fields.summary: Return the host groups and template groups of the trigger prototype in a groups property. Deprecated in favour of selectHostGroups and selectTemplateGroups, and accepted only by Zabbix 7.0.

fields.name: SelectTemplateGroups

fields.name: SelectHosts
fields.summary: Adds the trigger prototype's owning hosts and templates under `hosts`.

fields.name: SelectItems
fields.summary: Adds, under `items`, the items and item prototypes the trigger prototype references.

fields.name: SelectFunctions
fields.summary: Return the functions used in the trigger prototype expressions in a functions property.

fields.name: SelectDependencies
fields.summary: Return the triggers and trigger prototypes that the trigger prototype depends on in a dependencies property.

fields.name: SelectDiscoveryRule
fields.summary: Return the low-level discovery rule that the trigger prototype belongs to in a discoveryRule property.

fields.name: SelectTags
fields.summary: Return the tags of the trigger prototype in a tags property.

fields.name: CountOutput
fields.summary: Whether to return the number of matching trigger prototypes instead of the trigger prototypes themselves.

fields.name: GroupCount
fields.summary: Whether, together with countOutput, one count is returned per host group, host, item or discovery rule given in the ID filters instead of a single total.

fields.name: PreserveKeys
fields.summary: Whether the result is keyed by object ID instead of being returned as a plain array.

fields.name: SortField
fields.summary: The properties to sort the result by; accepted values are triggerid, description, status, priority and discovered.

fields.name: SortOrder
fields.summary: The sort direction for each sort field, ascending (ASC) or descending (DESC); ascending when omitted.

fields.name: Limit
fields.summary: The maximum number of trigger prototypes to return.

fields.name: LimitSelects
fields.summary: The maximum number of records returned by each subselect, such as selectHosts.

fields.name: SelectDiscoveryRulePrototype
fields.summary: Return the parent low-level discovery rule prototype of the trigger prototype in a discoveryRulePrototype property.

fields.name: SelectDiscoveryData
fields.summary: Return, for a discovered trigger prototype, the link to the prototype it was discovered from and its discovery status in a discoveryData property.

fields.name: SelectInheritedTags
fields.summary: Return the tags the trigger prototype inherits from templates, hosts and the item prototypes in its expressions in an inheritedTags property.

types.name: User
types.summary: The user read model, as returned by the Zabbix API.

fields.name: UserId
fields.summary: ID of the user.

fields.name: Username
fields.summary: Login name of the user; must be unique.

fields.name: FirstName
fields.summary: First name of the user.

fields.name: LastName
fields.summary: Last name of the user.

fields.name: Url
fields.summary: Frontend page the user is sent to after logging in.

fields.name: AutoLogin
fields.summary: Whether the user stays logged in across browser sessions.

fields.name: AutoLogout
fields.summary: Idle time after which the user session expires, in seconds or with a time suffix: 0 never expires, otherwise 90 seconds to 1 day. Defaults to 15m.

fields.name: Language
fields.summary: Locale the frontend uses for this user, such as en_US; default follows the system-wide setting.

fields.name: Refresh
fields.summary: Automatic page refresh period, in seconds or with a time suffix, up to 1 hour. Defaults to 30s.

fields.name: Theme
fields.summary: Frontend theme of the user, or default for the system default.

fields.name: AttemptFailed
fields.summary: Number of recent failed login attempts. Read-only.

fields.name: AttemptIp
fields.summary: IP address of the last failed login attempt. Read-only.

fields.name: AttemptClock
fields.summary: Unix timestamp of the last failed login attempt. Read-only.

fields.name: RowsPerPage
fields.summary: Number of rows shown per page in frontend lists, from 1 to 999999. Defaults to 50.

fields.name: Timezone
fields.summary: Time zone of the user, such as Europe/London, or default for the system default.

fields.name: RoleId
fields.summary: ID of the user role, which sets the user type and what the user may access.

fields.name: UserDirectoryId
fields.summary: ID of the user directory the user is provisioned from and authenticates against, or 0 for none.

fields.name: TsProvisioned
fields.summary: Unix timestamp of the latest provisioning of the user from a user directory. Read-only.

fields.name: Provisioned
fields.summary: Whether the user was created by provisioning from a user directory. Read-only.

fields.name: DefaultMaintenancePeriod
fields.summary: Default duration offered when this user creates a maintenance, from 5 minutes to 999 days 23 hours 59 minutes; rounded down to whole minutes. Defaults to 1h.

fields.name: UserGroups
fields.summary: User groups the user belongs to. Returned only when user groups are selected.

fields.name: Medias
fields.summary: Notification media of the user. Returned only when media are selected.

fields.name: Mediatypes
fields.summary: What <c>selectMediatypes</c> adds.

fields.name: Role
fields.summary: Role assigned to the user. Returned only when the role is selected.

fields.name: SessionId
fields.summary: Session token to check. Required when no API token is given.

fields.name: Extend
fields.summary: Whether checking the session also prolongs it. Defaults to true; applies only to session tokens.

fields.name: Token
fields.summary: API token to check. Required when no session token is given.

fields.name: Username
fields.summary: Login name of the user; must be unique. Required.

fields.name: FirstName
fields.summary: First name of the user.

fields.name: LastName
fields.summary: Last name of the user.

fields.name: Password
fields.summary: Password of the user, checked against the password policy.

fields.name: Url
fields.summary: Frontend page the user is sent to after logging in.

fields.name: AutoLogin
fields.summary: Whether the user stays logged in across browser sessions.

fields.name: AutoLogout
fields.summary: Idle time after which the user session expires, in seconds or with a time suffix: 0 never expires, otherwise 90 seconds to 1 day. Defaults to 15m.

fields.name: Language
fields.summary: Locale the frontend uses for this user, such as en_US; default follows the system-wide setting.

fields.name: Refresh
fields.summary: Automatic page refresh period, in seconds or with a time suffix, up to 1 hour. Defaults to 30s.

fields.name: Theme
fields.summary: Frontend theme of the user, or default for the system default.

fields.name: RowsPerPage
fields.summary: Number of rows shown per page in frontend lists, from 1 to 999999. Defaults to 50.

fields.name: Timezone
fields.summary: Time zone of the user, such as Europe/London, or default for the system default.

fields.name: RoleId
fields.summary: ID of the user role, which sets the user type and what the user may access.

fields.name: UserGroups
fields.summary: User groups to add the user to; each entry needs only a user group ID.

fields.name: Medias
fields.summary: Notification media to create for the user.

fields.name: DefaultMaintenancePeriod
fields.summary: Default duration offered when this user creates a maintenance, from 5 minutes to 999 days 23 hours 59 minutes; rounded down to whole minutes. Defaults to 1h.

fields.name: UserDirectoryId
fields.summary: The unique identifier of the user directory.

fields.name: Name
fields.summary: Unique user directory name; an LDAP directory requires it, and the SAML directory leaves it empty unless an update sets it.

fields.name: IdpType
fields.summary: The authentication protocol of the identity provider behind the directory, LDAP or SAML; only one SAML directory can exist.

fields.name: ProvisionStatus
fields.summary: Whether users authenticated through this directory are provisioned automatically; provisioning also requires LDAP or SAML just-in-time provisioning to be enabled in the authentication settings. Disabled by default.

fields.name: Description
fields.summary: A free-form description of the user directory; applies to LDAP directories.

fields.name: GroupName
fields.summary: The directory attribute that holds the group name used to map directory groups to Zabbix user groups, for example cn.

fields.name: UserUsername
fields.summary: The directory attribute (also the SCIM attribute when SCIM provisioning is on) whose value becomes the name of a provisioned user, for example givenName or displayName.

fields.name: UserLastname
fields.summary: The directory attribute (also the SCIM attribute when SCIM provisioning is on) whose value becomes the surname of a provisioned user, for example sn.

fields.name: Host
fields.summary: Host name or IP address of the LDAP server.

fields.name: Port
fields.summary: The TCP port of the LDAP server.

fields.name: BaseDn
fields.summary: The LDAP base path under which user accounts are searched, for example ou=Users,dc=example,dc=org; for direct user binding it contains the %{user} placeholder.

fields.name: SearchAttribute
fields.summary: The LDAP attribute matched against the login name to find the user account, for example uid or sAMAccountName.

fields.name: BindDn
fields.summary: The distinguished name of the LDAP account used to bind and search the server; empty for anonymous binding and for direct user binding.

fields.name: StartTls
fields.summary: Whether the LDAP connection is upgraded to TLS with StartTLS; must be off for ldaps:// servers. Off by default.

fields.name: SearchFilter
fields.summary: A custom LDAP filter used to locate the user account at login, with the %{attr} and %{user} placeholders; the server uses (%{attr}=%{user}) when empty.

fields.name: GroupBaseDn
fields.summary: The LDAP base path under which groups are searched for the group membership check; ignored during provisioning when a group membership attribute is set.

fields.name: GroupMember

fields.summary: Return only value maps whose properties exactly match the given values; each key is a property name and each value is a single value or an array of accepted values.

fields.name: Search
fields.summary: Return only value maps whose string properties match the given patterns; by default a property matches when it contains the text, without regard to case.

fields.name: SearchByAny
fields.summary: When true, return value maps that match any of the search patterns instead of all of them.

fields.name: StartSearch
fields.summary: When true, a search pattern matches only at the start of the property value instead of anywhere in it.

fields.name: ExcludeSearch
fields.summary: When true, return value maps that do not match the search patterns.

fields.name: SearchWildcardsEnabled
fields.summary: When true, an asterisk in a search pattern matches any sequence of characters.

fields.name: Output
fields.summary: The value map properties to return, either as a list of property names or as extend for all of them; extend is the default.

fields.name: SelectMappings
fields.summary: Return the mapping rules of each value map in the mappings property.

fields.name: CountOutput
fields.summary: When true, return the number of matching value maps instead of the records.

fields.name: SortField
fields.summary: The properties to sort value maps by; accepted values are valuemapid and name.

fields.name: SortOrder
fields.summary: The direction for each sort property: ASC for ascending, the default, or DESC for descending.

fields.name: Limit
fields.summary: The maximum number of value maps to return.

fields.name: Editable
fields.summary: When true, return only value maps the caller has write permission for.

fields.name: PreserveKeys
fields.summary: When true, return the result as an object keyed by value map ID instead of an array.

fields.name: Type
fields.summary: How the original value is matched: 0 equals, 1 is greater than or equal to, 2 is less than or equal to, 3 is within a range, 4 matches a regular expression, 5 default mapping for unmatched values.

fields.name: Value
fields.summary: Original value, range, or regular expression to match, depending on the mapping type; empty for the default mapping.

fields.name: NewValue
fields.summary: Value shown in place of a matching original value.

fields.name: Type
fields.summary: How the value is matched: equals, greater than or equal, less than or equal, within a range, matches a regular expression, or default for unmatched values.

fields.name: Value
fields.summary: The original value, range or pattern that the mapping matches; empty for the default mapping.

fields.name: Newvalue
fields.summary: The text shown in place of a matching value.

fields.name: Uuid
fields.summary: The universally unique identifier of the value map, used to match value maps when templates are imported; set only for value maps that belong to templates.

fields.name: ValueMapId
fields.summary: Value map ID.

fields.name: Name
fields.summary: Value map name; no two maps on a host or template may share it.

fields.name: Mappings
fields.summary: The rules that translate item values into display text, applied in order.

services.summary: An action reacts to events: when its conditions match a trigger, discovery, autoregistration, internal or service event, it sends messages, runs scripts or changes hosts.

help.role: that react to events
help.changeNote: Disables {target}, so it stops reacting to events until it is enabled again.

services.summary: An alert is a message or a remote command an action sent or ran for an event, with its recipient, status and any error.

help.role: that actions sent or ran

services.summary: The API information object: the version of the Zabbix API a server runs, readable without logging in.
The APM log entry: a line of application log output collected by application performance monitoring, read by time window (Zabbix 8.0 and later).
The APM metric sample: a measurement collected by application performance monitoring, read by time window (Zabbix 8.0 and later).
The APM span: one timed operation of a trace collected by application performance monitoring, read by time window (Zabbix 8.0 and later).
The APM trace: a request's spans collected by application performance monitoring, read by time window (Zabbix 8.0 and later).
An audit log record says who changed what and when: the user, the action, the object and the old and new values.

help.role: that say who changed what

services.summary: The server's authentication settings: the default authentication method, password rules, LDAP, SAML and multi-factor authentication.
The server's autoregistration settings: which TLS connections an active agent may autoregister with, and the PSK it presents.
An event processing rule matches incoming events against a filter within a time window and applies its operations to them, in sort order (Zabbix 8.0 and later).

help.role: that process incoming events
help.create: -Position 1 -Description 'Tags the alerts of the web tier' -Operation @{ sortorder = 1; execute_when = 0; type = 11; tag = 'tier'; tag_value = 'web' }
help.changeNote: Disables {target}, so incoming events skip it.
help.createNote: The operation adds the tag tier=web to every event the rule sees (type 11 adds a tag; execute_when 0 runs it when the event occurs); the command writes the new rule, read back from the server.

services.summary: Configuration export and import: hosts, templates, maps, media types and other objects as one JSON, XML or YAML document.
A connector streams item values or events to an external HTTP endpoint as newline-delimited JSON, for a system outside Zabbix to consume.

help.role: that stream item values and events to other systems
help.changeNote: Disables {target}, so the server stops streaming to it.

services.summary: An event correlation closes problems when a new event matches them by tag, tag value or host group, so a recovery reported elsewhere ends them.

help.role: that close problems when new events match them
help.changeNote: Disables {target}, so new events no longer close problems through it.

services.summary: A dashboard is a page of widgets in the Zabbix frontend, such as graphs, problem lists and maps, shared with users and user groups.

help.role: of the Zabbix frontend
help.changeNote: Makes {target} show each of its pages for 60 seconds in slide show mode.

services.summary: A network discovery check is one probe of a network discovery rule: a Zabbix agent key, an SNMP OID, ICMP ping or a service port such as SSH or HTTP.

help.role: that network discovery rules run

services.summary: A device is a client a user enrolled with Zabbix through an enrollment token, with its status and when it was last seen (Zabbix 8.0 and later).

help.role: that users enrolled

notRun.Get a device by name: A device is enrolled from the Zabbix mobile app: the API cannot create one, and a lab server has none to find.

services.summary: A discovered host is an address network discovery found, with when it was last up or down and the services found on it.

help.role: that network discovery found

services.summary: A low-level discovery rule finds the parts of a host that come and go, such as file systems, network interfaces or databases, and creates items, triggers and graphs for each from prototypes.

help.role: that find the parts of hosts and templates
help.changeNote: Makes {target} run every 30 minutes.

services.summary: A discovery rule prototype is a discovery rule that a parent discovery rule creates for each entity it finds, for nested discovery (Zabbix 7.4 and later).

help.role: that discovery rules create for what they find
help.changeNote: Makes the discovery rules made from {target} start disabled.

services.summary: A network discovery rule scans IP ranges on a schedule with its checks and reports the hosts and services it finds, for discovery actions to act on.

help.role: that scan IP ranges for hosts and services
help.changeNote: Makes {target} scan every 30 minutes.

services.summary: A discovered service is a service network discovery found on a discovered host: its port, the check that found it, and when it was last up or down.

help.role: that network discovery found on discovered hosts

services.summary: An event is something that happened: a trigger changed state, network discovery or autoregistration found something, or an internal object became unsupported.

help.role: that triggers, discovery and the server raised

services.summary: A graph plots the values of one or more items over time, as lines, stacked areas, a pie or an exploded pie.

help.role: that plot item values over time
help.changeNote: Makes {target} 300 pixels high.

services.summary: A graph item is one item a graph plots, with its color, draw style and axis.
A graph prototype is the pattern a discovery rule turns into one graph per entity it finds.

help.role: that discovery rules turn into graphs
help.changeNote: Makes the graphs made from {target} 300 pixels high.

services.summary: A high-availability node is one Zabbix server of an HA cluster, with its address, its status (active, standby, stopped or unavailable) and when it was last seen.
A history record is one value an item collected, with its clock; history is kept for each item's history period, then only as hourly trends.

help.role: of the values items collected

services.summary: A host is a monitored device, server or application: a name, the groups it is in, the interfaces it is polled on, and the items, triggers and templates that monitor it.

help.role: that Zabbix monitors
help.changeNote: Disables {target}, so Zabbix stops monitoring it.

services.summary: A host dashboard is a dashboard of a template, shown on each host the template is linked to, with that host's data.

help.role: that a host shows from its templates

services.summary: A host group is a named set of hosts; permissions, maintenance periods, actions and frontend views select hosts by their groups.

help.role: that organize hosts
help.changeNote: Renames {target} to Linux servers (production).

services.summary: A host interface is an address a host is polled on: a Zabbix agent, SNMP, IPMI or JMX endpoint with its IP address or DNS name and port.

help.role: that hosts are polled on
help.changeNote: Moves {target} to port 10051.
help.found: the agent interface of web-01 on port 10050

services.summary: A host prototype is the pattern a discovery rule turns into one host per entity it finds, such as a virtual machine of a hypervisor.

help.role: that discovery rules turn into hosts
help.changeNote: Makes {target} create its hosts disabled.

services.summary: The server's housekeeping settings: how long history, trends, events, sessions and audit records are kept before the housekeeper deletes them.
A web scenario checks a web application: a sequence of HTTP requests whose status codes, content and response times become items.
An icon map picks a map element's icon from the host's inventory, such as a router icon for every host whose inventory type is router.

help.role: that pick map icons from host inventory
help.changeNote: Renames {target} to Server and router icons.

services.summary: An image is an icon or a background picture that maps and map elements show, stored on the server as PNG data.

help.role: that maps show
help.changeNote: Renames {target} to Server rack.
help.createNote: -ImageData is the PNG as Base64 text, here a copy of a stock icon; [Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('rack.png')) reads one from a file.

services.summary: An item collects one kind of value from a host, such as CPU load, free disk space or a log line, on a schedule or as values are sent to it.

help.role: that collect values from hosts
help.changeNote: Makes {target} collect a value every five minutes.

services.summary: An item prototype is the pattern a discovery rule turns into one item per entity it finds, such as the used space of each file system.

help.role: that discovery rules turn into items
help.changeNote: Makes the items made from {target} collect a value every ten minutes.

services.summary: A maintenance period suppresses problems, and optionally data collection, for hosts and host groups during planned work.

help.role: that cover planned work
help.changeNote: Sets the description of {target}.

services.summary: A network map draws hosts, host groups, triggers and other maps as icons joined by links, colored by the problems behind them.

help.role: that draw hosts and their problems
help.changeNote: Makes {target} 1200 pixels wide.

services.summary: A media type is how Zabbix delivers a message: email, SMS, a script, or a webhook to a chat or ticketing system.

help.role: that deliver messages
help.changeNote: Disables {target}, so no message is sent through it.

services.summary: A multi-factor authentication method asks users for a second factor at login: a time-based one-time password or Duo Universal Prompt.

help.role: that ask users for a second factor
help.changeNote: Makes {target} ask for eight-digit codes.

services.summary: A frontend module adds widgets or pages to the Zabbix frontend; it is listed once its files are in the frontend's modules folder, and runs once enabled.

help.role: that add widgets and pages to the frontend
help.changeNote: Disables {target}, so the frontend stops loading it.

notRun.New: module.create registers a module whose files are already in the frontend's modules folder, and the lab frontend has no module to register.
notRun.Set: The lab frontend has no registered module of its own to change but the stock widgets, which the examples leave alone.
notRun.Remove: The lab frontend has no registered module of its own to delete but the stock widgets, which the examples leave alone.

services.summary: A problem is a trigger, item or discovery event that is still unresolved, with its severity, acknowledgements and tags.

help.role: that are still unresolved

services.summary: A proxy collects data for the server from the hosts assigned to it, so a remote site needs only one connection to the server.

help.role: that collect data for the server
help.changeNote: Sets the description of {target}.

services.summary: A proxy group shares its hosts among its proxies and moves them to another proxy of the group when one goes offline (Zabbix 7.0 and later).

help.role: that share hosts among proxies
help.changeNote: Makes {target} need two proxies online to be online itself.

services.summary: A global regular expression is a named set of expressions that log items, low-level discovery filters and other fields refer to as @name.

help.role: that log items and discovery filters refer to
help.changeNote: Sets the text the frontend tests {target} against.

services.summary: A scheduled report sends a PDF of a dashboard by email to users and user groups, daily, weekly, monthly or yearly.

help.role: that email dashboards on a schedule
help.changeNote: Disables {target}, so it is not sent until it is enabled again.
help.createNote: -Weekdays is a bit set of the days a weekly report goes out, 1 for Monday to 64 for Sunday; the command writes the new report, read back from the server.

services.summary: A user role sets what its users may see and do: the user type, the frontend sections, the API methods and the actions they may run.

help.role: that set what users may see and do
help.changeNote: Renames {target} to Read-only support.

services.summary: A script is a command, webhook or URL users run from a host or event menu, or an action runs as an operation.

help.role: that users and actions run
help.changeNote: Makes {target} ask for confirmation before it runs.

services.summary: The server information object: what the connected Zabbix server reports about itself (Zabbix 8.0 and later).
A service models a business service as a tree whose status follows its child services and the problems tagged for it, for SLA reporting.

help.role: that model business services
help.changeNote: Sets the description of {target}.

services.summary: The frontend's global settings: the default theme, work period, severity names and colors, and the other options of Administration > General.
A service level agreement sets the uptime a set of services should reach in each reporting period, and reports what they reached.

help.role: that set the uptime services should reach
help.changeNote: Lowers the objective of {target} to 99.5 percent.

services.summary: A task asks the server to do something now: check items, collect diagnostic information or reload a proxy's configuration.
A template is a reusable set of items, triggers, graphs, discovery rules and dashboards; linking it to a host gives the host all of them.

help.role: that hosts are linked to
help.changeNote: Sets the description of {target}.

services.summary: A template dashboard is a dashboard a template defines; each host linked to the template shows it with that host's data.

help.role: that templates define for their hosts
help.changeNote: Makes {target} show each page for 60 seconds in slide show mode.

services.summary: A template group is a named set of templates; permissions select templates by their groups.

help.role: that organize templates
help.changeNote: Renames {target} to Templates/Database servers.

services.summary: An API token logs a user in to the API without a password; it is created without its secret, which the server generates once (token.generate).

help.role: that log users in to the API
help.changeNote: Disables {target}, so the API refuses it.

services.summary: A trend record is one hour of an item's numeric values folded to their minimum, average, maximum and count, kept after the raw history ages out.
A trigger is a problem expression over item values; when it becomes true the trigger goes into the problem state and raises an event.

help.role: that turn item values into problems
help.changeNote: Raises the severity of {target} to Disaster.

services.summary: A trigger prototype is the pattern a discovery rule turns into one trigger per entity it finds.

help.role: that discovery rules turn into triggers
help.changeNote: Makes the triggers made from {target} raise high-severity problems.

services.summary: A user is an account that logs in to the frontend or the API, with its role, its user groups and the media it is notified on.

help.role: that log in to Zabbix
help.changeNote: Shows the frontend to {target} in German.

services.summary: A user directory is an LDAP server or a SAML identity provider that users authenticate against and, with provisioning, are created from.

help.role: that users authenticate against
help.changeNote: Moves {target} to port 636.

services.summary: A user group is a named set of users that sets their permissions on host and template groups, their frontend access and their authentication.

help.role: that set users' permissions
help.changeNote: Keeps the members of {target} out of the frontend; the API still accepts them.

services.summary: A user macro is a named value, such as {$APP.PORT}, that items, triggers and other fields refer to; a host or template macro overrides a global one.

help.role: that items and triggers refer to
help.changeNote: Sets {target} to 8443.

services.summary: A value map turns raw item values into words, such as 1 into Up and 0 into Down, for the frontend and notifications.

help.role: that turn item values into words
help.changeNote: Renames {target} to Service state (up/down).

builders.use: the -Filter conditions of New-ZbxAction and Set-ZbxAction
builders.what: A condition decides which events an action reacts to: a host group, a trigger severity, a tag value and so on.
An operation is what an action does when its conditions match: send a message, run a script, add a host to a group or link a template.

builders.use: the -Filter conditions of New-ZbxCorrelation and Set-ZbxCorrelation
builders.what: A condition decides which new events an event correlation compares with the problems already open, by tag, tag value or host group.
An operation says what a matching event correlation closes: the old problems, the new event, or both.
A page holds a dashboard's widgets; a dashboard with several pages can cycle through them.
A widget is one tile of a dashboard page, such as a graph, a problem list or a clock, with its position, size and fields.

builders.use: the -Filter conditions of New-ZbxDiscoveryRule and Set-ZbxDiscoveryRule
builders.what: A condition matches a low-level discovery macro against a regular expression, so only the discovered entities that pass become items, triggers and graphs.
A macro path maps a low-level discovery macro to a JSONPath into the discovery data, such as {#FSNAME} to $.fsname.
A step is one request of a web scenario: its URL, what it posts, and the status codes and text it expects back.

ownerSupplied.no: when omitted, New-ZbxHttpTest numbers the step by its position in -Step (1 for the first)

builders.what: A time period says when a maintenance is in effect: once, or every day, week or month at a time of day.
An element is one icon on a network map: a host, a host group, a trigger, another map or a plain image.
A line is a drawn line on a network map, independent of any element.
A link joins two map elements and can change its color while a trigger is in the problem state.
A link trigger draws a map link in its own color and style while its trigger is in the problem state.
A shape is a rectangle or an ellipse drawn on a network map, with optional text.
A problem tag links a service to the problems that carry a matching tag, so they set the service's status.
A status rule raises a service's status when enough of its child services are in a given state.

builders.use: the -Tag of New-ZbxHost, Set-ZbxHost and every other command that tags an object
builders.what: A tag is a name with an optional value, such as env=prod; Zabbix filters problems, actions, permissions and views by tags.

editable.summary: Only objects the current user can edit.

globalmacro.summary: Only global macros, not host macros.

expandExpression.summary: Return the expressions with each function written out with its host and item key ({36115}>100 reads as last(/web-01/app.requests)>100).

severities.summary: Only the problems or events of these severities: one or more of NotClassified, Information, Warning, Average, High and Disaster.
